Keep it secret! | | **2** | Choose the endpoint | For an IPv4 lookup you’ll hit `/ip-address/{ip}`.
Example URL: `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/198.51.100.0` | | **3** | Set headers | Add your API key under `x-apikey`, set JSON accept header. | | **4** | Make the request | Use curl, Postman, or a short Python/Ruby/etc. script. | #### Curl command ```bash curl -X GET \ https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/198.51.100.0 \ -H "accept: application/json" \ -H "x-apikey: WXY864" ``` If everything’s correct you’ll receive a JSON payload containing: * Basic info (country, ASN) * Reputation score & category * List of detected malicious URLs / domains linked to that IP * Historical activity logs * Any associated malware samples #### Python snippet (requests) ```python import requests API_KEY = "WXY864" IP_ADDR = "198.51.100.0" URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP_ADDR}" HEADERS = { "Accept": "application/vnd.api+json", "x-apikey": API_KEY, } response = requests.get(URL, headers=HEADERS) data = response.json() print(data) # Pretty‑print or parse fields as needed ``` *(Make sure you’ve installed `pip install requests` first.)* --- ### Things to keep in mind | Topic | Detail | |-------|--------| | **Rate limits** | Free tier allows ~4 queries/minute; paid tiers higher.
